item.title: 2025 GenAI Security Readiness Report: A Clearer Picture of Where Enterprises Stand
item.description:
Author: Lakera Team
Date: October 31, 2025
Tags: ["Generative AI", "Enterprise Security", "AI Risk Management", "Cybersecurity", "Technology Adoption"]
Summary:
  • GenAI is widely adopted in enterprises by 2025.
  • Security readiness is lagging behind adoption.
  • Many organizations lack AI-specific security expertise.
  • Common risks include prompt injections and data leakage.
  • The report recommends proactive risk management and training.
  • Integrated AI security frameworks are essential for future safety.

item.title: 5 Agentic AI Strategies for Risk Management
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: October 31, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Risk Management", "AI Governance", "Cybersecurity", "Compliance"]
Summary:
  • Agentic AI acts autonomously at superhuman speed.
  • This creates new risks for privacy and compliance.
  • Organizations must apply governance and human oversight.
  • Continuous monitoring and red teaming reduce risks.
  • Structured frameworks like NIST AI RMF help manage risks.
  • Risk management builds trust and prevents failures.

item.title: AI Model Risk Management: Key Types and Mitigation Strategies
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: October 31, 2025
Tags: ["AI Risk Management", "AI Governance", "Compliance and Ethics", "Model Security", "AI Lifecycle Management"]
Summary:
  • AI model risk management identifies and mitigates risks in AI throughout its lifecycle.
  • Risks include ethical, operational, security, and compliance issues.
  • Continuous testing and governance ensure model reliability and accountability.
  • Global standards like NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act guide risk management.
  • Effective management combines people, processes, and technology.
  • It helps maintain trustworthy and compliant AI systems.

item.title: OpenAI’s Santosh Vempala Explains Why Language Models Hallucinate
item.description:
Date: October 24, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Natural Language Processing", "Machine Learning", "AI Research", "Language Models"]
Summary:
  • Santosh Vempala explains why language models hallucinate.
  • Hallucinations arise during pre-training due to data limitations.
  • They are linked to misclassification and statistical calibration.
  • Models often produce plausible but incorrect facts.
  • Current training methods struggle to fix hallucinations.
  • Future research aims to improve uncertainty expression and reduce errors.

item.title: ServiceNow’s Tara Bogavelli on AgentArch: Benchmarking AI Agents for Enterprise Workflows
item.description:
Author: Tara Bogavelli
Date: October 24, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Machine Learning", "Enterprise Software", "Benchmarking", "AI Research"]
Summary:
  • ServiceNow developed AgentArch to benchmark AI agents in enterprise workflows.
  • It tests planning, tool use, and memory in realistic settings.
  • AgentArch moves beyond static Q&A benchmarks.
  • Maintaining coherence across steps is a key challenge.
  • The benchmark simulates tasks like customer service and IT operations.
  • This helps improve AI for real-world production environments.

item.title: Top LLM Tracing Tools
item.description:
Date: October 30, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Large Language Models", "AI Lifecycle Management", "Generative AI", "AI Evaluation Tools"]
Summary:
  • 82% of enterprise leaders use generative AI weekly as of October 2025.
  • Many face challenges scaling AI agents in production.
  • LLM tracing tracks inputs and outputs inside AI models.
  • It helps identify performance issues and optimize efficiency.
  • Tracing is vital for complex AI agents using multiple tools.
  • Top tools exist to support full LLM pipeline management.
